<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The Maven Surefire test group filter is hardcoded.

The hardcoded `!ai-eval` group filter may prevent the command-line `-Dgroups=ai-eval` from overriding the Surefire configuration. This needs verification.

Maven user properties override POM plugin parameters that declare a `property` attribute. The command-line `-Dgroups=ai-eval` will therefore replace the hardcoded `!ai-eval` filter.

Eval tests will use plain JUnit 5 without Spring context. They will call the ask endpoint via HttpClient and support a configurable base URL. The Q1 scenario checks for grounded results, Payment ticket citations, and payment failure mentions.

Payment tickets cannot be identified by category alone, since responses omit that field. The test will instead check that returned ticket IDs fall within the TKT-1001–TKT-1005 range. For the payment-failure mention requirement, a case-insensitive substring check on the generated answer will be used rather than an exact string match.

Q2 will verify TKT-1001 is grounded and cited, while checking the answer does not fabricate resolution text absent from the seed data.

Q3 will require grounded results containing at least one Shipment ticket from TKT-1006–TKT-1010.

Q4 will confirm cited tickets carry a RESOLVED or CLOSED status.

Q5 will validate that sources are strictly drawn from TKT-1001–TKT-1005 and are limited to HIGH priority payment-related rows.

Response status is present but priority is missing. The seed SQL will reveal which tickets are HIGH priority. O1–O5 will return exact no-match bodies.

Q2 will avoid fragile resolution-text assertions. It will only verify TKT-1001 is grounded and cited. Q1 will check for grounded results, at least one Payment ticket citation, and a lowercase answer containing "payment".

Q3 will require grounded results containing at least one Shipment ticket from TKT-1006–TKT-1010.

Q4 will enforce that every cited source carries a RESOLVED or CLOSED status.

Q5 will restrict sources to TKT-1001 and TKT-1002, treating those as the sole HIGH priority payment tickets. If the model cites additional payment tickets, the test will flag the discrepancy against the retrieval scores.

The Q1 payment-failure check will look for "payment" plus either "fail" or "declin" to catch paraphrased answers. If the model cites a medium-priority ticket and the test fails, the assertion may need loosening to the documented set.

The eval strategy serves as the acceptance criteria. Keyword checks will match documented pass criteria without requiring exact generated text.

A system prompt is being drafted to enforce grounding. It instructs the assistant to answer only from the provided ticket context and to refuse general knowledge.

The debug log only records chunks that pass the threshold, so rejected candidates remain invisible. Calibration suggests lowering the threshold only if an in-scope question misses an expected ticket whose score falls slightly below 0.6.

To see which stronger tickets were rejected, the threshold must be lowered or the database queried directly. Temporarily setting the similarity threshold to 0.0 and restarting the service would expose all top-k scores for calibration.

A direct SQL cosine distance query against the vector store is preferable to changing committed code. The plan is to generate the question embedding via Ollama’s embed API and compute exact similarity scores in Postgres. This reveals exactly which stronger tickets were rejected by the 0.6 threshold.

Checking Spring AI’s PgVectorStore source to confirm the exact cosine distance formula. This ensures the manual SQL query against the vector store will return comparable similarity scores for calibration.

Spring AI 1.0 PgVectorStore computes cosine similarity as `1 - (embedding <=> ?)`. Rather than manually extracting the SQL from the JAR, the faster calibration path is to pass `--app.rag.similarity-threshold=0` on the command line and restart the service. This exposes all top-k scores instantly.

Lowering the threshold risks pulling in low-score junk. The real problem is that the model ignored the retrieved ticket entirely. I need to inspect the raw model output to see why grounding failed.

A critical bug may be misinterpreting Spring AI’s cosine score. If the framework returns distance instead of similarity, a score of 0.625 would mean high distance and poor match. The threshold of 0.6 would then reject the best candidate while keeping poor matches. This would explain why TKT-1005 passed yet the model still failed to ground. The next step is to restart with threshold 0 to inspect raw scores and verify whether the metric is distance or similarity.

The 0.625 score for TKT-1005 is plausible if the metric is similarity, since weaker embeddings without the search_query prefix would push other tickets below the cutoff. If the metric were distance, the sole passing document would be the least similar, and Spring AI would have discarded more similar candidates. Because the threshold is passed directly to Spring AI, the framework itself may be misapplying the filter.

Spring AI documentation confirms similarityThreshold filters by similarity >= threshold, converting distance to similarity internally. PgVectorStore embeds queries internally, so raw question prefixes cannot be injected. Low raw scores are expected without prefixes, and calibration will lower the threshold if the best candidate still falls below the cutoff. The next step is to query Postgres directly for exact distances.

```bash
def embed(text):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://localhost:11434/api/embed",
        data=json.dumps({"model": "nomic-embed-text", "input": text}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)["embeddings"][0]

def rank(label, text):
    vec = "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.8f}" for x in embed(text)) + "]"
    sql = f"""
select metadata->>'ticketId' as ticket,
       metadata->>'sourceType' as section,
       round((1 - (embedding <=> '{vec}'::vector))::numeric, 4) as similarity
from vector_store
order by embedding <=> '{vec}'::vector
limit 8;
"""
    print(f"\n=== {label} ===")
    subprocess.run(["docker", "exec", "-i", "ticket-management-system-postgres-1", "psql", "-U", "tickets", "-d", "tickets"], input=sql.encode(), check=True)

rank("payment failures", "Have we seen payment failures before?")
rank("capital of france", "What is the capital of France?")
PY
```

```bash
node << 'JS'
const pages = await (await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list")).json();
const page = pages.find((p) => p.type === "page");
const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
let nextId = 1;
const pending = new Map();
function send(method, params = {}) {
  const id = nextId++;
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
  });
}
ws.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {
    const waiter = pending.get(msg.id);
    pending.delete(msg.id);
    if (msg.error) waiter.reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error)));
    else waiter.resolve(msg.result);
  }
});
await new Promise((resolve) => ws.addEventListener("open", resolve));
await send("Runtime.enable");
await send("Page.enable");
await send("Page.navigate", { url: "http://localhost:5173/tickets/TKT-1001" });
const started = Date.now();
let text = "";
while (Date.now() - started < 10000) {
  const result = await send("Runtime.evaluate", { expression: "document.body.innerText", returnByValue: true });
  text = result.result.value || "";
  if (text.includes("Payment declined at checkout") && !text.includes("Loading ticket")) break;
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
}
console.log(text.slice(0, 500));
ws.close();
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The Maven `-Dgroups=ai-eval` flag failed to override the POM's default test groups.

The POM groups property needs to be set to `!ai-eval` and referenced via `${groups}`. This lets the command-line `-Dgroups=ai-eval` override the default. The test run confirms the eval suite was excluded.

The better approach is to configure the Maven Surefire plugin directly. Setting `<excludedGroups>ai-eval</excludedGroups>` in the plugin configuration avoids relying on a Maven property expansion.

Hardcoding `<groups>!ai-eval</groups>` in the POM prevents the CLI `-Dgroups` flag from overriding it. The fix is to define a Maven property such as `<surefire.groups>!ai-eval</surefire.groups>` and reference it via `${surefire.groups}` in the Surefire configuration. This allows the command-line flag to override the default.

The Maven property must be named `groups` for the CLI flag `-Dgroups=ai-eval` to override it. The POM will be updated to define `<properties><groups>!ai-eval</groups></properties>` and reference it via `<groups>${groups}</groups>` in the Surefire configuration. This resolves the T033 issue where the property was incorrectly set in phase two.

The fix belongs in the polish phase because the eval command cannot work otherwise. After updating the POM, I will run `mvn test -Dgroups=ai-eval` to confirm the eval suite executes. I will also run a targeted normal test to verify the default exclusion still works.
</details></think>

```bash
python3 << 'PY'
import json, urllib.request, subprocess

def embed(text):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://localhost:11434/api/embed",
        data=json.dumps({"model": "nomic-embed-text", "input": text}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)["embeddings"][0]

def rank(label, text):
    vec = "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.8f}" for x in embed(text)) + "]"
    sql = f"""
select metadata->>'ticketId' as ticket,
       metadata->>'sourceType' as section,
       round((1 - (embedding <=> '{vec}'::vector))::numeric, 4) as similarity
from vector_store
order by embedding <=> '{vec}'::vector
limit 6;
"""
    print(f"\n=== {label} ===")
    subprocess.run(["docker", "exec", "-i", "ticket-management-system-postgres-1", "psql", "-U", "tickets", "-d", "tickets", "-c", sql], check=True)

questions = [
    ("Q2 resolution TKT-1001", "What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?"),
    ("Q3 shipment", "What are the common causes of shipment tracking issues?"),
    ("Q4 resolved", "Show me similar resolved tickets."),
    ("Q5 high priority payment", "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?"),
    ("O1 weather", "What is the weather in Paris today?"),
    ("O2 stock", "What is the stock price of Apple?"),
    ("O3 bread", "How do I bake sourdough bread?"),
    ("O5 missing", "What was the resolution for TKT-9999?"),
]
for label, text in questions:
    rank(label, text)
PY
```

```bash
python3 << 'PY'
import json, urllib.request, subprocess

SYSTEM = """You answer questions about support tickets using only the ticket context in the user message.
Use only facts that appear in that context. Do not use outside knowledge.
Cite every ticket you rely on by its ticket id (TKT- followed by digits) exactly as shown in the context header.
If you cite a ticket, the id must appear in the context. Do not cite any ticket id that is not in the context.
If the context does not contain enough information to answer, say that the tickets do not contain the answer and do not invent facts.
"""

def embed(text):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://localhost:11434/api/embed",
        data=json.dumps({"model": "nomic-embed-text", "input": text}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)["embeddings"][0]

def top_chunks(question, n=5):
    vec = "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.8f}" for x in embed(question)) + "]"
    sql = f"""
select content from vector_store
order by embedding <=> '{vec}'::vector
limit {n};
"""
    out = subprocess.check_output(["docker", "exec", "-i", "ticket-management-system-postgres-1", "psql", "-U", "tickets", "-d", "tickets", "-At", "-c", sql])
    return out.decode()

def chat(question):
    chunks = top_chunks(question)
    user = "Ticket context:\n" + chunks.strip() + "\n\nQuestion:\n" + question
    body = {
        "model": "llama3.1:8b",
        "stream": False,
        "options": {"temperature": 0},
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": user},
        ],
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://localhost:11434/api/chat",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:
        data = json.load(resp)
    print("\n====", question)
    print(data["message"]["content"])

chat("What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?")
PY
```

```bash
python3 << 'PY'
import json, urllib.request
questions = [
    "What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?",
    "What are the common causes of shipment tracking issues?",
    "Show me similar resolved tickets.",
    "What is the weather in Paris today?",
    "What is the capital of France?",
    "What was the resolution for TKT-9999?",
    "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?",
]
for q in questions:

        "http://localhost:8080/api/ai/ask",
        data=json.dumps({"question": q}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},

    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:

    sources = [(s["ticketId"], s["status"], round(s["score"], 3)) for s in body["sources"]]
    print(f"\nQ: {q}")
    print("grounded", body["grounded"], "sources", sources)
    print("answer", body["answer"][:300].replace("\n", " "))
PY
```

```bash
python3 << 'PY'
import json, urllib.request
questions = [
    "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?",
    "What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?",
    "Show me similar resolved tickets.",
    "Have we seen payment failures before?",
    "What is the capital of France?",
    "What was the resolution for TKT-9999?",
    "What are the common causes of shipment tracking issues?",
]
for q in questions:
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://localhost:8080/api/ai/ask",
        data=json.dumps({"question": q}).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:
        body = json.load(resp)
    sources = [(s["ticketId"], s["status"], round(s["score"], 3)) for s in body["sources"]]
    print(f"\nQ: {q}")
    print("grounded", body["grounded"], "sources", sources)
    print("answer", body["answer"][:240].replace("\n", " "))
PY
```
